swap_risks: CRITICAL SUPPLY VOLTAGE RATING: LMV358IDR is limited to 5.5 V max (5.5 V abs max, p.5) whereas LM358DR2G supports up to 30 V (32 V abs max, p.3). Installing a 5.5 V CMOS part on a 12 V–24 V rail causes instant breakdown.

HIGH HEADROOM / CLIPPING RISK: Rail-to-rail capability differs (LM358DR2G: IN=Non-RR, OUT=Non-RR vs LMV358IDR: IN=Non-RR, OUT=RR); verify input common-mode range (Vicm) and output voltage swing against ADC full-scale range.

CAUTION QUIESCENT CURRENT SHIFT: Supply current per channel differs by 3.3x (LM358DR2G: 350 µA/ch p.4 vs LMV358IDR: 105 µA/ch p.7); verify battery budget and total power dissipation across all channels.
HIGH ABSOLUTE-MAX SURGE MARGIN: LMV358IDR has a lower Vs,abs,max rating (5.5 V, p.5) than LM358DR2G (32 V, p.3); verify hot-plug, inductive kickback, and TVS clamp peaks stay safely below 5.5 V.

HIGH TEMPERATURE GRADE MISMATCH: Rated ambient range differs (LM358DR2G: 0..70 °C Commercial (0°C to +70°C) vs LMV358IDR: -40..125 °C Extended Industrial (-40°C to 125°C)); LM358DR2G cold limit only 0 °C, LM358DR2G hot limit only 70 °C — verify product ambient qualification before swapping.
engineering_verdict: LM358DR2G (onsemi, SOIC-8) and LMV358IDR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required alternatives: the PCB land pattern is compatible, but passive retuning or rating derating is mandatory because supply voltage Vs,max drops >=20%; rail-to-rail input/output swing differs; quiescent supply current Iq/ch differs 3.3x. Signal-chain deltas: GBWP 1 MHz (p.6) vs 1 MHz (p.7), supply ceiling 30 V (p.4) vs 5.5 V (p.5), Vos 7 mV (p.4) vs 7 mV (p.7), Ib 3x gap (45000 vs 15000 pA). Primary bench gotchas to watch: LM358DR2G "CRITICAL ESD Trap: Standard onsemi LM358DR2G Is Rated ONLY 250 V HBM / 100 V MM (p.3)!" (p.3) and LMV358IDR "5.5 V Absolute Maximum Ceiling — Destructive If Swapped into LM358 High-Voltage Boards" (p.5). BOM decision: Choose LM358DR2G when supply rails exceed 5.5 V (rated up to 30 V); choose LMV358IDR when ultra-low supply current (105 µA/ch) is prioritized. Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.1 vs TOP_VIEW p.3) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
